chapter: Basie and life on the road
title: Family at home and women on the road
summary: Strain of marriage and children when touring; infidelity on the road.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Was there a problem when you were on the road, having a family? Family back home? Oh, yeah. What were some of the problems having a family back home?

When you were on the road? I would say yes and no to that. Problem then no problem. You see, now, like, my wife, as long as I was on the road, we were all right. If I come home for a week or two, everything's all right. But when I quit a band and come back home, we can't get along. We can't make it.
I don't know. Like, women get tired of seeing you. But when you go out, everything is all right when you come back. But you stay there a long time. She's going to start fuzzing and nagging at you.
Any other problems? What about, did you have any kids during all this time? Well, how does it affect your kids?

Well, see, my kid, I had two kids, my second wife had two kids, and when we divorced, even before we broke up, I met another woman, and she had two children. So I kept my oldest daughter, and the other woman helped me to raise her, my daughter told me we got divorced, and we got married. And she raised my daughter from two years old to about thirteen. Then we divorced. And she was married. But it's hard one way to be married and traveling. It's easy. See, because no matter how long you stay with a woman and you're married, you're going to have some good days when you first come home. But after you be around her, it looks like she gets, it looks like she don't want to be bothered with you anymore. Like you, like, see, because some of those women, they're getting used to being by themselves. They don't have anybody to tell them when to go and when to stay. Right, right. And you come home and say, well, look, baby, where you going? I ain't no business with you. Nobody asked me where I'm going. I'm going out. Well, where you going out with? You don't have to know.
So they've had so much independence when you're out of town.
Yeah. But see, I used to mess around on the road, but when I come home, I want to be with my wife.

So you would see women on the road? Oh, yeah. Oh, okay. But was that kind of, was it common? I mean, guys on the road had wives, but then they- Yeah, you know, like, it's hard, it's hard. Play two lives, so to speak.
It's hard to travel like that, you know, with a popular band, and you were popular too, for you not to have women that hit on you.

Women come over there and, and like some places we would go, women, they had certain instruments that they like. Where's the trumpet player? Oh, you're going to be my man for the night. Some guys, some women say, I want the guitar player, I want the drummer. Every band that comes along, she's a drummer. She likes drummers. Every band that comes along, she wants the drummer.
